title: Virtual fundamental classes, part II: integral and non-separated Chow theory of Deligne–Mumford stacks and virtual classes over general bases
summary: Integral Chow groups of Deligne–Mumford stacks of finite type over any field without separatedness, their degrees and integral operations; for stacks with a proper cover, rational pushforward, Gysin maps and Chern classes on stacks; comparisons with the scheme, algebraic-space and separated rational groups; intersection rings, moduli spaces, the ring structure of the Edidin–Graham comparison and degrees of points; the virtual class without the resolution property and for stacks with a proper cover, the relative obstruction class and characterisations, relative formulas over pure-dimensional bases, relative invariance of Vistoli's rational equivalence, regular pullback and functoriality over reduced bases, deformation invariance, and the perfect relative obstruction theory of relative spaces of maps from prestable curves.

layers.title: Proper covers, function fields and degrees

targets.name: StackChow.ProperCover
targets.statement: A proper cover of a stack M is a scheme X of finite type over k with a proper surjective (hence representable) morphism X -> M; for integral M a proper covering is one with X integral and X -> M generically finite. Every stack with a separated finite-type morphism to a Noetherian scheme (in particular every separated stack) has a proper cover, generically finite with X quasi-projective; an integral stack with a proper cover has a proper covering; proper covers pass to closed and open substacks, along morphisms representable by schemes, to vector bundles and products, and from M' to M along a proper representable surjection M' -> M.
hypotheses: M a Deligne-Mumford stack of finite type over a field k with quasi-compact separated diagonal representable by schemes (Convention 1)

api.name: ProperCover.restrict
api.statement: A proper cover of M restricts to closed and open substacks and to stacks representable by schemes over M, and composes with a proper representable surjection onto M.

api.name: ProperCover.covering_exists
api.statement: An integral M with a proper cover has a proper covering; two proper coverings are dominated by an integral closed subscheme of their fibre product surjecting onto both (vistoli1989 lines 1610-1613).

api.name: ProperCover.of_separated
api.statement: A stack with a separated finite-type morphism to a Noetherian scheme has a generically finite proper cover by a quasi-projective scheme (deligne-mumford1969 Theorem 4.12).

targets.name: StackChow.functionField
targets.statement: For an integral stack V, k(V) is the colimit over nonempty open substacks of morphisms to A^1, a field finitely generated over k with trdeg = dim V, identified for an etale U -> V from an integral scheme with the rational functions on U with equal pullbacks to U x_V U; e(V) is the order of the automorphism group of a geometric point over the generic point, equal to the degree of the inertia over a dense open where it is finite etale; e(V) = 1 iff V has a dense open substack that is an algebraic space.
hypotheses: V an integral stack (Convention 1; integral closed substacks of gap closed-substacks-of-stacks)

targets.name: StackChow.stackDegree
targets.statement: For a separated dominant morphism f : F -> G of integral stacks, deg(F/G) in Q>=0 is deg(F x_G V/V) for representable f (V etale over G integral; generic rank, 0 if not generically finite) and deg(U/G)/deg(U/F) in general (U etale over F integral affine); it is independent of choices, multiplicative, equal to (e(G)/e(F))[k(F):k(G)] with [E:K] = 0 for infinite extensions, positive iff dim F = dim G, integral for representable f, and invariant under dominant base change with integral fibre product.
hypotheses: f separated and dominant
F, G integral stacks, not necessarily separated

layers.title: Intersection rings, moduli spaces, quotients and points

targets.name: StackChow.intersectionProduct
targets.statement: For M smooth of pure dimension n with a proper cover, x . y := Delta^!(x x y) (Delta a regular local immersion of codimension n), and x ._f y := gamma_f^!(x x y) for f : F -> G with G smooth; A^*(M)_Q is a commutative associative graded Q-algebra with unit [M], flat representable pullback between smooth stacks with proper covers is a ring map, g_*(g^*x . y) = x . g_*y for proper representable g, and on smooth schemes this is SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.6's product (x) Q. For smooth separated M of pure dimension and representable T -> M, every class in VirtualFundamentalClass §2.5's A^*(T -> M) commutes with all bivariant classes and evaluation on [M] is an isomorphism A^*(T -> M) = A_*(T)_Q.

targets.name: StackChow.moduliSpace_pushforward_iso
targets.statement: Let M have a proper cover and p : M -> M0 be proper onto a quasi-separated algebraic space of finite type inducing bijections on isomorphism classes of geometric points (a moduli space). hypotheses: M has a proper cover
p proper, bijective on geometric points up to isomorphism
M0 quasi-separated algebraic space of finite type

suppliers.what: The base roadmap: stack dimension, cones and normal cones, Vistoli's rational Chow theory of separated stacks with bivariant groups and the canonical rational equivalence, relative cotangent complexes, cone stacks and h1/h0, intrinsic normal cones, obstruction theories, the virtual class of separated stacks with the resolution property, compatible pullback and functoriality over smooth bases, and the relative class; through gap:closed-substacks-of-stacks, the integral closed substacks of its §2.1.

Algebraic spaces and stacks, inertia, points, separated and proper stacks, quotient stacks, coarse spaces and Keel–Mori, quasi-coherent cohomology and its topology comparison, derived categories, the upper shriek functor and relative dualising complexes, Riemann–Roch on curves, lifting for smooth morphisms, and the Chow theory of schemes.
The Edidin–Graham comparison A_{i-g}([X/G])_Q = A^G_i(X) (x) Q for Deligne–Mumford quotient stacks, with Chern classes and proper pushforward.
Equivariant Chow groups by Totaro's approximation, their operations and the equivariant product (Conventions 1, 4, 5).
Coherent cohomology and base change of proper curve families, the relative dualising sheaf, relative ampleness, prestable families.
Derived tensor and internal Hom on ringed sites, the pullback–pushforward adjunction, quasi-coherent derived sheaves and base change.
The naive truncation of the cotangent complex of a surjection, the smooth computation, and square-zero lifting obstructions for ring maps.

consumers.what: Its §§4.1–4.3 are the case of 9.3–9.5 over the prestable-curve stack with a smooth projective target in characteristic zero; 6.2 removes its use of the resolution property; 8.4 gives deformation invariance; 5.4 computes degrees on coarse spaces.

gaps.title: Closed, reduced and integral closed substacks of a Deligne–Mumford stack
gaps.detail: VirtualFundamentalClass §2.1 builds its cycles on integral closed substacks but its contract does not state their theory. Needed, with no separatedness: closed substacks as representable closed immersions up to equivalence, equivalently invariant closed subschemes of an étale presentation (vistoli1989 (1.5), lines 232–244); reduced, irreducible, integral ones (vistoli1989 (1.6), lines 245–250); the unique reduced closed substack on a closed subset of |M| (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 Stacks.points) and the bijection of integral closed substacks with irreducible closed subsets; base change; images under proper morphisms with a proper cover of the source, under proper representable morphisms and under flat morphisms (vistoli1989 (1.7), lines 254–269).
gaps.needs: VirtualFundamentalClass §2.1 must state the theory of closed, reduced and integral closed substacks of a Deligne–Mumford stack, with reduced induced structures, the support bijection, base change and images, without separatedness.
